problemStatement.formal: \liminf_{n \to \infty} (p_{n+1} - p_n) \leq H \text{ for some explicit constant } H
problemStatement.plain: AVAILABLE: There exist infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes differing by at most H. Zhang proved H ≤ 70,000,000 in 2013; Maynard improved to H ≤ 600; Polymath project achieved H ≤ 246; assuming Elliott-Halberstam conjecture H ≤ 12. The Twin Prime Conjecture (H=2) remains open.
whyMatters: Zhang's 2013 breakthrough was the first proof that prime gaps are bounded, resolving a century-old open problem
The Polymath project (Tao et al.) reduced the bound to 246 via massive collaborative optimization
The gap H ≤ 12 conditional on Elliott-Halberstam gives compelling evidence for the Twin Prime Conjecture

proven: Conditional on Elliott-Halberstam: lim inf (p_{n+1} - p_n) ≤ 12
Engelsma's explicit 50-tuple with diameter 246 is admissible
GPY theorem (2005): lim inf g_n / log p_n = 0
open: Twin Prime Conjecture: infinitely many p with p+2 also prime
de Polignac conjecture: for each even k, infinitely many prime gaps equal k
Optimal H in the unconditional Polymath bound
Removing Elliott-Halberstam assumption to get H ≤ 12
knownResults.goal: Formalize the bounded prime gaps theorem with the Polymath 246 bound, and document the mathematical landscape around it.
